record.paper_title: The Hamiltonian Seifert Conjecture: Examples and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Size of the aperiodic energy-value set
record.original_question: Let (W, ω) be a symplectic manifold with bounded Hofer–Zehnder capacity, meaning that every open subset U \subset W with compact closure has finite Hofer–Zehnder capacity, and let H: W → R be a smooth proper Hamiltonian. If A^P_H denotes the set of regular values a for which the energy level {H = a} carries no periodic orbit of the Hamiltonian flow, how large can A^P_H be? In particular, beyond the fact that almost-existence theorems force A^P_H to have measure zero, what kinds of zero-measure sets can occur as the full set of regular aperiodic values?

evidence.quote: Now we are in a position to state the main question considered in this paper. We call a value a of H aperiodic if the level {H = a} carries no periodic orbits. Let W be a symplectic manifold of bounded capacity and H a smooth proper function on W. How large can the set APH of regular aperiodic values of H be?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(W,\omega)$ be a symplectic manifold. Recall that the Hofer–Zehnder capacity $c_{HZ}(U)$ of an open set $U\subset W$ is defined as the supremum of $\max H - \min H$ over all smooth, compactly supported, "admissible" Hamiltonians $H\colon U\to\mathbb{R}$ (those whose Hamiltonian flow has no non-constant periodic orbits of period at most $1$). We say that $(W,\omega)$ has bounded Hofer–Zehnder capacity if every open subset $U\subset W$ with compact closure satisfies $c_{HZ}(U)<\infty$.

Let $H\colon W\to\mathbb{R}$ be a smooth proper function. A regular value $a$ of $H$ is called aperiodic if the level set $\{H=a\}$ carries no periodic orbits of the Hamiltonian vector field $X_H$ defined by $\iota_{X_H}\omega = -dH$. Denote by $\mathcal{A}^P_H\subset\mathbb{R}$ the set of regular aperiodic values of $H$.

It is known (almost-existence theorems) that, under the bounded Hofer–Zehnder capacity hypothesis, $\mathcal{A}^P_H$ has Lebesgue measure zero. The problem is: how large can $\mathcal{A}^P_H$ be? In particular, characterize which measure-zero subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ can arise as $\mathcal{A}^P_H$ for some such $W$ and $H$. For instance, must $\mathcal{A}^P_H$ always be nowhere dense, countable, or discrete?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of how large the set of regular aperiodic values of a proper Hamiltonian on a symplectic manifold of bounded Hofer–Zehnder capacity can be remains open. Known counterexamples to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture (smooth in $\mathbb{R}^6$ by Ginzburg, $C^2$-smooth in $\mathbb{R}^4$ by Ginzburg–Gürel) produce aperiodic regular levels but only on discrete sets of energy values, while almost-existence only forces measure zero. The gap between "discrete" (all known examples) and "measure zero" (the general bound) has not been closed.

status_evidence.title: A C^2-smooth counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in R^4
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a proper C^2 function on R^4 with a regular level carrying no periodic orbits of the Hamiltonian flow.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples exist producing aperiodic regular levels, but only at isolated energy values.

status_evidence.title: A smooth counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in R^6
status_evidence.snippet: Smooth proper function on symplectic R^6 with a non-singular level set carrying no periodic orbits.
status_evidence.claim: Known examples produce only discrete aperiodic value sets, leaving the size question open.

status_evidence.title: The Hamiltonian Seifert Conjecture: Examples and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: In all known examples of Hamiltonian flows on linear spaces such energy values form a discrete set, whereas almost existence theorems only require this set to have zero measure.
status_evidence.claim: The question of how large the aperiodic value set can be is explicitly posed as open.
